item.title: 'It Follows' Star Officially Addresses Her Return to Another Iconic 2010s Thriller Franchise
item.dc:creator: Maria Loreto
item.description: In a new interview, Maika Monroe addressed whether or not she'd return for a sequel to one of her most beloved movies.
item.content:encoded: Maika Monroe has built a career as a modern scream queen. After a breakout 2014, when she starred in both It Follows and The Guest, she became a key figure in horror, continuing to revisit the genre in everything from Longlegs to Victorian Psycho. This year, both It Follows and The Guest have been a part of the horror conversation: It Follows just wrapped a sequel, wonderfully titled They Follow, while The Guest just received a quasi-sequel with Onslaught, which director Adam Wingard set in the same continuity as his previous 2014 film.

item.title: The Wendy’s JRPG Is a Searing Anti-Capitalist Screed About Humans Making Real Art
item.dc:creator: Ari Notis
item.description: WendyQuest, also known as the "Wendy's JRPG," is developed by the very real humans at 81Monkeys, known for the in-progress World of Anterra.
item.content:encoded: Over the past year, Wendy’s — yes, the same Wendy’s known for its square burgers, thick milkshakes, and unlikely stewardship of a mid-tier donut chain — has made waves through a series of unconventional creative partnerships. Amid slumps in sales and attention, Wendy’s has turned to popular artistic mediums, like music and video games, to try and reverse course.

item.title: Xbox Game Pass November 2026 Lineup Announced
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: Escape Academy 2 and Warhammer Survivors headline Microsoft's latest Xbox Game Pass additions arriving in November.
item.content:encoded: Xbox Game Pass subscribers have another batch of games to look forward to as Microsoft expands its subscription library with new additions throughout November. The latest announcement includes everything from a new co-op escape room adventure to a minimalist kingdom-building strategy game and a bullet-heaven spin-off set in the Warhammer universe.

item.title: Ubisoft Makes Bid to Purchase Xbox Studio on the Brink of Closure
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.description: Ubisoft and other companies have reportedly made offers to buy Arkane from Xbox, which is looking to divest from the Marvel's Blade studio.
item.content:encoded: Microsoft intends to divest from Dishonored and Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Studios as part of its mass layoffs at Xbox and other Microsoft divisions. Because Arkane is based in Lyon, France, Xbox has had to adhere to French labor laws, and was mandated to search for a potential buyer for Arkane.

item.title: Mass Effect Fans Are Trying to Make This N7 Day the Biggest One Ever
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.description: Mass Effect fans are asking players on every platform to boot up the games together on Saturday, Nov. 7, from 2 to 5 p.m. ET, for N7 Day
item.content:encoded: The fan group We Are Mass Effect is asking players on any platform to boot up a Mass Effect game at the same time on Saturday, Nov. 7, from 2 to 5 p.m. ET (11 a.m. to 2 p.m. PT, 7 to 10 p.m. GMT and 8 to 11 p.m. CET). The idea is to see as many people as possible playing at once to truly demonstrate (with data!) how many of us love and are still actively enjoying Mass Effect.

item.title: WoW: Forever's Beta Was Pure Magic. No One Knows What Happens Next
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: World of Warcraft: Forever, which launches on Nov. 4, is a brilliant reinvention of the classic MMO by Blizzard
item.content:encoded: I only took the character to level 6, however. I realized that this was the character I'd want to play and the path I'd want to follow in the live game when it launches this week, on Nov. 4, and I didn't want to spoil that experience. At the same time, I felt a professional obligation to check out Forever's brand-new race, the Skyborne elves, and their flying-island starting zone, Zephras Isle. So I started again, with a Skyborne Druid.

item.title: Magic: The Gathering Is Reprinting a Powerful $30 Sword With Perfect Pixel Art
item.dc:creator: Chris Guest
item.description: Truth, justice... and polygons?
item.content:encoded: Magic: The Gathering is reaching into its inventory of powerful artifacts to reprint a sword worth nearly $30, complete with gloriously nostalgic video game artwork. Sword of Truth and Justice, a popular Equipment first released in 2019, is returning in a new Secret Lair collection that draws inspiration from the blocky, polygonal graphics of the Nintendo 64 and original PlayStation era.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Meets God of War Ragnarök in Upcoming Steam Action Game Hit
item.dc:creator: Ari Notis
item.description: Tides of Annihilation plays a whole lot like Black Myth: Wukong, Phantom Blade Zero, and other stylish action games out of China's gaming scene.
item.content:encoded: Right now, the gaming world is obsessed with Phantom Blade Zero. S-Game’s Wuxia-inspired action game landed as one of the highest-rated games of 2026 and immediately tore up the charts on Steam, cracking 800,000 concurrent players on launch weekend. I’m enjoying Phantom Blade Zero, even if it does have a few too many parries for my taste. But it’s primarily made me more excited about a similar, promising game I briefly played earlier this year: Tides of Annihilation.

item.title: Sony Pushes PS5 Owners To Trade In Consoles Amid Unprecedented Price Hikes
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: Sony pursues new trade-in options as prices for PS5 consoles surge, but fans are unsure if it's a good deal
item.content:encoded: The future of affordable video game consoles is not looking good, and hardware makers like Sony know it. The PlayStation 5 has undergone two major price hikes while the Xbox Series X has jumped in price three times in a single year. The AI-driven VRAM crisis at the heart of the issue is expected to worsen. Given the supply constraints, Sony has limited options for selling PS5s at prices customers might find acceptable.

item.title: For GTA 6, Xbox Put an Xbox Series X in an Alligator
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: Xbox has unveiled the Series X-BITE, a working Xbox Series X swallowed by a custom alligator. Here's how to enter the giveaway.
item.content:encoded: Xbox has come up with a rather unusual way to celebrate Florida wildlife ahead of the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 launch, unveiling a custom Xbox Series X that looks like it has been swallowed whole by an alligator. Even stranger, the console inside actually works, and one lucky fan could soon have the bizarre gaming accessory sitting in their home.

item.title: D&D’s World of Warcraft Crossover Is the Bold Shake-Up the Game Needed
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: D&D’s World of Warcraft crossover delivers inventive character options and tougher boss fights that breathe new life into high-level play.
item.content:encoded: Wizards of the Coast has been playing things safe since updating the rules of Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition in 2024. After lead designers Jeremy Crawford and Chris Perkins left Wizards in 2025 to join Critical Role’s Darrington Press, Wizards slowed the pace of new D&D releases. Recent books have focused mostly on updating the lore and rules for the game’s most popular campaign settings and rebalancing previously published character options. D&D’s newest release bucks the trend, delivering an ambitious collection of innovative character options, monsters, and ways to use some of the game’s less developed subsystems. It just requires venturing to a new world.

item.title: PC Games Storefront Does What Valve Won’t, Takes Action Against AI Slop
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez
item.description: One of Steam's biggest competitors just announced filtering options for AI-generated content.
item.content:encoded: The game industry is in the middle of a huge uptick in AI-generated content. A whopping 54.6% of titles added to Steam in October 2026 included an AI disclosure label, marking the first month that more games had the label than not. For comparison, 18.3% of games added to the platform in 2025 had an AI disclosure label.

item.title: Zach Cregger's Sci-Fi Masterpiece Made One Brilliant Change to Its Monster: 'It Just Looks Creepier'
item.dc:creator: Jake Kleinman
item.description: Resident Evil's VFX team reveals the secrets behind the Pedestrian, Mutant Bryan, and more
item.content:encoded: In the weeks after the release of Resident Evil, a viral clip showed several acrobatic performers tied together at the waist and practicing the movements of the mutated, cartwheeling mass of limbs known as the "Pedestrian" in Cregger's adaptation of the horror video game franchise. This has led some people online to assume that the creature in the film was actually a practical effect, with a bit of CGI on top. But as Smith explains, that is an incorrect assumption.

item.title: 'GTA 6' Early Preload Times And File Size Confirmed By Rockstar
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: Rockstar Games reveals when GTA 6 fans can begin preloading the highly-anticipated open-world adventure and how much hard drive space they'll need
item.content:encoded: We're officially in the last stretch before the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 on Nov. 19, and though it's closer than ever, for some, the wait has become all the more excruciating. The good news is that you can start planning to play GTA 6 the second it becomes available — and you can start those preparations earlier than anticipated.

item.title: Bethesda Officially Confirms The Elder Scrolls 6 Name
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: Todd Howard officially reveals The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel in video celebrating Bethesda's 40th anniversary
item.content:encoded: Bethesda has finally revealed the name of the next Elder Scrolls game. The long-awaited RPG will be titled The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel. Just a few days ago, fans of the series started theorizing this would be the title and now it's confirmed. Todd Howard made the announcement in a video celebrating Bethesda Softworks' 40th anniversary.

item.title: Xbox Game Pass’ Newest Addition Is a Near-Perfect Couch Co-Op Game
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School delivers lots of clever co-op escape room puzzles that are especially great for couples.
item.content:encoded: Thanks to a multiplayer renaissance, we’re currently living in a golden age of couples games. Whether you and your significant other are playing Split Fiction or pairing up for Big Walk, there are no shortage of great trust-building co-op games out there currently. You can add another great option to the list, thanks to Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School, a near-perfect new inclusion to couch co-op canon.

item.title: Nintendo Officially Comments on Zelda Remake's Divisive Graphics
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has a divisive graphical style. Nintendo explains the art direction behind the Switch 2 game.
item.content:encoded: Nintendo's upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time looks drastically different from the Nintendo 64 original. That's understandable, given the nearly 28 years that have passed since the first 3D Zelda debuted. Beyond the graphical advancements, however, the Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time makes some bold character design choices, some of which have divided longtime Zelda fans.

item.title: Dead by Daylight Fans Are Uninstalling the Game in Protest
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: Behavior Interactive gifted Vtuber TheBurntPeanut all Dead by Daylight DLC, a controversial decision the community didn't take lightly.
item.content:encoded: Some Dead by Daylight players are expressing disappointment with developer Behaviour Interactive — and vowing to uninstall the game — after the studio appeared to show support for divisive streamer TheBurntPeanut.

item.title: 2024's Best Action Game Is (Mostly) Just as Good in Stunning Switch 2 Port
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.description: Stellar Blade and its top-notch action have been ported to Nintendo Switch 2. It plays great, though in handheld mode its visuals falter at times.
item.content:encoded: Shift Up’s Stellar Blade is one of the decade’s great action games, blending together quick-paced sword combat and powerful parries. A sequel is on the way, but before it arrives, Shift Up isn’t done with the first game. It arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 later this week, the latest in a long line of satisfying Switch 2 ports, even if it shares the same issues as most of them.

item.title: A Terrifying Survival Take On Jurassic Park Is Coming to Steam Next Week
item.dc:creator: Ford James
item.description: Wilderdark, a survival horror game set on a dinosaur-infested island, is coming to Steam on Tuesday, Nov. 10.
item.content:encoded: For some reason, there haven't been that many truly great dinosaur video games throughout history. Ark: Survival Evolved had plenty of success despite the fact it was quite janky, and The Isle has spawned myriad viral videos thanks to its proximity chat. Jurassic World Evolution 3 is by far the best licensed dinosaur game, but it focuses on managing the theme park, as opposed to fighting and surviving.

item.title: One of the GameCube’s Great Cult Classics Gets the Remaster It Deserves
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.category: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered
item.description: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Remastered is a faithfully clumsy revival of a cult classic that's still a casual joy to play.
item.content:encoded: When I was a kid, there were some games I only knew through magazines. I never played them, but they were all over the pages of Electronic Gaming Monthly and Nintendo Power, so I knew everything about them anyway. Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee was firmly a “magazine game” when it was released for the GameCube in 2002. I even had a free poster of it on my wall as a kid, one I kept hung up even after a wave of middling reviews eventually dropped.

item.title: Hideo Kojima's Next Game Officially Gets New Teaser Image, Fans Already Hunting for Clues
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez
item.description: Kojima Productions released a new teaser image of OD for the studio's 10th anniversary exhibition.
item.content:encoded: More than four years after its initial announcement, OD remains one of the biggest mysteries in the video game industry. We know Kojima Productions’ next game is some sort of horror experience, and that genre auteur Jordan Peele contributed to the project, butspecifics are hard to come by. Despite the caginess, we got a new look at OD as part of Kojima Productions’ 10th anniversary exhibition, which is running through Dec. 20 at Azabudai Hills Gallery in Tokyo.

item.title: 9 Ways Mina the Hollower Was as Complex and Audacious to Make as Any AAA Game
item.dc:creator: Matt Patches
item.description: Ahead of awards season, we asked the folks at Yacht Club Games how the sausage was made
item.content:encoded: David D'Angelo, programmer at Yacht Club Games: Mina actually started with, Alec, the director, as a side project. He wanted to get better at doing art stuff. He said, “I'm gonna make a little game where I could make Game Boy Color art.

item.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Studio Officially Revealed
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: Nintendo has finally revealed which developer is working on the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
item.content:encoded: Nintendo is infamously cagey about revealing which studios are working on its games. While the company’s secrecy isn’t entirely out of step with an industry that generally hides how the sausage is made, Nintendo takes this to another level, trying to create a Disneyland-like sense of wonder around its brand.

item.title: FF14’s New Expansion Officially Addresses Dawntrail’s Biggest Problem
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: Final Fantasy 14 Evercold will fix the MMORPG's pacing problem seen in the Dawntrail expansion
item.content:encoded: None ofFinal Fantasy 14's expansions so far are overtly awful, but there are some that don't quite hit the highs of others. That was the case for 2024's Dawntrailexpansion, which had the unenviable task of being the first part of the MMORPG's new arc. One major criticism from players fell on the story's pacing, which could admittedly be all over the place. For Evercold, the next expansion, Square Enix is making it a point to fix this.

item.title: Forget ‘Crystal Lake,’ the Best Action Thriller in TV History Remains Unbeaten 29 Years Later
item.dc:creator: Maria Loreto
item.description: Crystal Lake gives Linda Cardellini’s Pamela Voorhees a fun, bloody showcase, but a ’90s series still has TV’s best action.
item.content:encoded: Crystal Lake has been dominating the streaming charts. Over the past week, the series became Peacock’s fourth most-watched scripted original. It inspired hundreds of online videos analyzing its twists and turns, and reminded the world of the everlasting magic of Linda Cardellini.

item.title: Quentin Tarantino’s First New Movie in 7 Years Officially Arrives in Theaters Next Month
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.category: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
item.description: The Once Upon a Time in Hollywood universe returns with a new crime thriller from David Fincher and Quentin Tarantino, arriving on Netflix next month.
item.content:encoded: Quentin Tarantino fans have spent the better part of seven years waiting to see what one of the best filmmakers in the industry might do next. Since the Oscar-winning Once Upon a Time in Hollywood hit theaters in 2019, Tarantino has kept himself busy with books, interviews, and plans for what he once described as his final film. That milestone was initially meant to arrive in 2024 with The Movie Critic, but Quentin Tarantino famously shelved the script before production could begin, leaving fans in the dark about what could come next. But that's about to change next month.

item.title: Penguin Colony was made to 'put the games industry on notice'
item.dc:creator: Matt Patches
item.description: Why the Xbox boycott and Palestinian crisis fuel Penguin Colony, a penguin adventure game set among Lovecraft's horrors.
item.content:encoded: The latest game from Origanme Digital (Umurangi Generation) reimagines H.P. Lovecraft's At the Mountains of Madness through the eyes of Antarctica's indigenous inhabitants, transforming a seemingly absurd premise into a deeply personal work of psychological horror. For Tali Faulkner, a Māori developer from New Zealand, the monsters of Penguin Colony aren't nearly as frightening as the real-world atrocities that inspired them.

item.title: Fable Is Ditching the One Feature That Made Fable 3 An Instant Classic
item.dc:creator: Ari Notis
item.description: Playground Games' Fable reboot will be a purely single-player game, ditching an important part of what made the originals so great.
item.content:encoded: The original Fable checked all of the boxes of a good fairy tale: a classic good-versus-evil tale set in a high-fantasy version of Fake Britain. You played as a hero (literally, the “Hero of Oakvale”) fighting against a guy who considered burning down villages his idea of a good time. Fable’s big innovation lay in its morality system: Depending on your actions, the hero’s appearance would change (ex: you’d grow devil horns if you were evil), as would the way the citizens of Albion would react to him. Just like the main characters of stories like Jack and the Beanstalk, Little Red Riding Hood, and other quintessential fairy tales, you were consigned to live with the consequences of your actions — good or bad.

item.title: The best local co-op games to play in 2026
item.dc:creator: Ford James
item.description: Two-player co-op games like Split Fiction and Lego Voyagers are the perfect fit for a cozy fall weekend.
item.content:encoded: As we approach the colder months, it's becoming the time when sitting inside and playing some of the best local co-op games is looking more and more appealing. Even though couch co-op and split-screen play is often pushed to the side in favor of online co-op, there are still plenty of modern games that allow players to sit side-by-side and play together. And believe it or not, some of those games are great!

item.title: Doom Creator John Romero Revives Xbox-Canceled Game At New Publisher
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: Romero Games' next shooter has found a new publisher, although the scope of the project has drastically changed since Xbox dropped it
item.content:encoded: The fate of the next game from Doom creator John Romero was in jeopardy after Xbox canceled the project last year. Thankfully, Romero confirmed in a new interview that the project will see the light of day, as his studio has found another publisher.

item.title: A Persona 1 Remake Is In Development, New Leak Suggests
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: Persona games really do have a bad habit of leaking ahead of their reveals, as gameplay of a Revelations: Persona remake has surfaced
item.content:encoded: Persona 4 Revival and Persona 6 aren't even out yet, and another Persona game has already leaked. Fittingly for Halloween, some new footage of an in-development Persona remake emerged online. It appears to be for a remake of Revelations: Persona, the first game in the series.

item.title: Itch.io Reveals Just How Much AI Slop Is Flooding Gaming Storefronts
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: The number of new game pages being created daily has doubled in the past two months, itch.io confirmed
item.content:encoded: A quick glance at Steam or itch.io shows how gaming storefronts are flooded with new games as more developers use generative AI, making it harder than ever for indie devs with hand-crafted games to stand out. A recent social media post by itch.io revealed some new data highlighting just how bad the situation has become.

item.title: New Fortnite Item Makes Everything on the Item Shop Completely Free
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: There's a rare item in Fortnite that grants free Item Shop cosmetics for two weeks, as part of the new One Piece season.
item.content:encoded: Fortnite Treasure Hunters is here at last. This season is all about pirates and plundering treasure. Players can look the part using the Straw Hat Pirates skins from One Piece. It can get expensive to purchase cosmetics in Fortnite, but this season, there's an in-game item that makes everything in the Item Shop free. It almost sounds too good to be true, but it's real, and it's out there on the Battle Royale island.

item.title: Dungeons & Dragons Turned Hansel and Gretel Into a Near-Perfect Adventure
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: A delicious one-shot sends players to a candy cottage
item.content:encoded: Most of the published adventures for Dungeons & Dragons focus on epic fantasy, tasking players with fighting ancient necromancers, rampaging demons, or invading armies in order to prevent some great calamity. But the stakes don’t have to be so high to have a great session, and a bit of whimsy can prove just as memorable as a dramatic battle. That’s why one of my favorite adventures from Wizards of the Coast is a silly fairy tale inspired by Hansel and Gretel.

item.title: Welcome to the New Era of Video Game Adaptations
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: A week filled with updates on upcoming video game adaptations proves that Hollywood's latest trend is here to stay.
item.content:encoded: Buckle up, because that trend is about to kick into full gear. This week, we got a flood of news stories confirming that Hollywood is in a full-on gold rush. The film rights to video games are currently getting snapped up at an alarming rate. While that’s not exactly new for an industry that has a long history of eyeing game movies that never pass the scripting phase, we’re actually seeing significant developments that signal an approaching tidal wave.

item.title: 10 Video Games With the Best Twist Endings Nobody Saw Coming
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.description: From Spec Ops: The Line to Link’s Awakening, these 10 video games have the best twist endings, with reveals that recast everything before them.
item.content:encoded: The best twist endings in video games change what you thought you were playing. A great one makes you want to start over to spot the clues, and a perfect one hides those clues in plain sight: in dialogue, in chapter titles, perhaps even the controller you’re holding. These ten games span three decades and nearly every genre, from horror to puzzle-platformers to a Game Boy adventure about a dream. But they all have one thing in common: Every one of them had us totally fooled the first time.

item.title: 5 Must-Play Nintendo Switch 2 Games Coming in November 2026
item.dc:creator: Jen Glennon
item.description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and Metaphor: ReFantazio lead a strong month for Nintendo Switch 2 game releases
item.content:encoded: November is typically a major month for video game releases, and 2026 is no exception. The biggest game of the month is undoubtedly Grand Theft Auto 6, which is one of the most anticipated entertainment events of all time. But Rockstar’s magnum opus isn’t coming to Switch 2 — not yet, anyway. That said, there are still plenty of intriguing new games coming out for Nintendo’s hybrid console in November. Here are five that we’re especially excited about.

item.title: 5 Best Nintendo Switch Games That Desperately Need Switch 2 Upgrades, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: Many Nintendo Switch games received upgrades for Switch 2, but here are five classic Nintendo Switch games that did not.
item.content:encoded: The Nintendo Switch 2 has been on one heck of run through launch. Though it has yet to see new installments of some heavy-hitter franchises, Nintendo’s latest console has built up an impressive library of games over its first year and a half. A chunk of that list includes excellent Nintendo Switch 2 Editions of the Switch’s best games. Super Mario Bros. Wonder, Kirby and the Forgotten Land, and more have gotten substantial updates that have helped make great Nintendo games even better. That trend is continuing too, as evidenced by the upcoming Pikmin 4 — Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy.

item.title: 10 Classic '90s RPGs That Have Aged Like Fine Wine, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Ashley Potter
item.description: RPGs from the 1990s were some of the most pivotal games in history. Here are 10 classic 1990s RPGs that are so good they don't need a remake.
item.content:encoded: The 1990s proved a pivotal decade for gaming, fueled by technological advancements and new businesses that would go on to leave a lasting impact on the industry. The '90s saw the release of both the original Sony PlayStation (1995) and the Nintendo 64 (1996) which brought iconic titles such as Super Mario 64,Resident Evil, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

item.title: Every Resident Evil Game, Ranked From Worst to Best
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: We've ranked every mainline Resident Evil game, from the original all the way through 2026's Resident Evil Requiem.
item.content:encoded: After decades of misses, 2026 gave us one of the best gaming adaptations of all time. Well, sort of. Zach Cregger’s take on Resident Evil was a hit among critics who have praised the horror movie for its delightfully playful tone. The only catch is that it didn't have much to do with the established lore and characters of the actual Resident Evil games. Instead, it told its own story in the universe, which is probably for the better, considering how complicated the game saga gets.

item.title: 6 Essential Activities GTA Needs to Let Players Experience in Vice City
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: GTA 6's side activities seem expansive, but I hope Rockstar leaves room for these, too
item.content:encoded: GTA 6 is just around the corner, and despite Rockstar releasing quite a lot of footage over the last month, I still think there's very little to show what we'll actually be doing in the game. Crime, yes. The usual spate of side activities, yes. Having sex, apparently. But there's still a lot of room for speculation about what you can do in those in-between moments. I hope some of these activities make the cut.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Just Killed Crimson Desert's Chances At a GOTY
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: Phantom Blade Zero has rave reviews, tons of buzz, and a preferential release date, effectively boxing Crimson Desert out of GOTY 2026.
item.content:encoded: Phantom Blade Zerois off to a roaring start. The Wuxia action game by S-Game started the week with strong reviews and ended it with stratospheric player numbers on Steam, where the Chinese audience can be relied upon to turn out for a big release from their native country.

item.title: Skyblivion's Biggest Legal Challenge Yet Is Not Coming From Bethesda
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: As Skyblivion nears release, a former volunteer is trying to sue those working on the mod bringing The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion to Skyrim
item.content:encoded: Skyblivion, an ambitious mod aiming to recreate all of The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion within Skyrim's game engine, has run into a new legal challenge after over a decade of volunteer-driven development. Surprisingly, these legal troubles don't stem from Bethesda Game Studios or Microsoft, but a former volunteer.

item.title: 'No Man's Sky' Players Pay Homage To Star Trek's Patrick Stewart
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: No Man's Sky players are honoring late Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart by naming planets and star systems after him.
item.content:encoded: Patrick Stewart was a celebrated actor whose career spanned decades of film, television, and theater. He became a household name playing Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, but his work also included decades of live performances with the Royal Shakespeare Company and memorable roles as Gurney Halleck in Dune (1984) and King Richard in Robin Hood: Men in Tights (1993). But, of course, for millions of fans, he'll always be Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation.

item.title: Warframe officially adds a whole new star system in December
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: Warframe will leave the Origin System and head to Tau before the end of the year
item.content:encoded: Before the end of the year, Warframe will get a whole lot bigger. The Warframe: Tau expansion will be released for free in December and adds its namesake star system to the live service shooter alongside a lot of other new content.

item.title: Walmart Gives Surprise Gift Cards Over Canceled Zelda Switch 2 Orders
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: Walmart was unable to fulfill every special Ocarina of Time Switch 2 order and is now trying to make up for it with $519 gift cards.
item.content:encoded: On Thursday, Nintendo released a special edition of the Nintendo Switch 2 in anticipation of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which is set to launch Nov. 5. As with most special hardware releases, the Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary-themed Switch 2 sold out quickly. Walmart oversold the consoles and found itself having to cancel orders a day before launch.
